title: String length primitive
rationale: Delphi `Length(S)` on a string returns the number of characters, not bytes. Rust `&str` is UTF-8, so `.len()` would return the byte count and diverge for non-ASCII input; `.chars().count()` returns the Unicode scalar count, the closest match to Delphi's per-character semantics. The result is cast `as i32` because Delphi `Length` returns a signed Integer. The string parameter maps to a borrowed `&str` (no ownership transfer is implied by reading a length). Only {op0} is referenced; the duplicated second operand in the fact is ignored by this shape.
